message.content:
Let  
\[
I = \int -3*exp(x)*cos(x)\,dx
\]

We can use the standard antiderivative:
\[
\int exp(x)*cos(x)\,dx = \frac{1}{2}*exp(x)*(sin(x)+cos(x))
\]

Therefore,
\[
I = -3*\left(\frac{1}{2}*exp(x)*(sin(x)+cos(x))\right)+C
\]

Simplifying:
\[
I = -\frac{3}{2}*exp(x)*(sin(x)+cos(x))+C
\]

Equivalently:
\[
I = -\frac{3}{2}*exp(x)*sin(x) - \frac{3}{2}*exp(x)*cos(x)+C
\]

<answer>-3/2*exp(x)*sin(x) - 3/2*exp(x)*cos(x) + C</answer>
